about: Filter catalog keyed by OTD Path. Property names match OTD settings.json exactly (C# property names, not UI labels: OTD silently ignores unknown names). 'default' is the plugin's own default (from its source); 'min'/'max' are sensible osu! tuning bounds used to clamp recommendations (they may be narrower than what the plugin accepts). 'stage': 'raw' = OTD 0.6.8 PipelinePosition.Internal (runs before every pre-transform filter); in OTD 0.6.x PipelinePosition.Raw is an alias of PreTransform, so former 'raw' filters are 'pre'. Inside one stage OTD runs filters in the order of the profile's Filters list: the engine never reorders a user's chain by stage. 'auto_recommend' false = never chosen by the engine (user decision only); 'policy_note' is the i18n key of the note shown to the user. 'homepage' is where the plugin can be found (the program never installs plugins). 'notes' are developer notes, never shown to the user (user text lives in locales/*/engine.json under summary_key / added_latency_note). Sources: docs/research/filters.md (audit 2026-10-30).

filters.notes: Source-verified (TabletDriverFilters master, shipped as HawkuFilters 0.3.1.0): namespace OpenTabletDriver.Plugin, class NoiseReduction, PluginName 'Hawku Noise Reduction', PreTransform, millimetre coordinates. Samples (UI 'Buffer') default 10, setter clamps 0..20; DistanceThreshold default 0.5 mm, setter clamps 0..10. One-step weighted geometric median of the buffer; output = median while the new point is within DistanceThreshold, blends toward raw between 1x and 2x threshold, buffer reset to raw at >= 2x. Tooltip: recommended Samples 5-20, threshold 0.2-1.0 mm; ~75 ms max latency at 133 rps with buffer 10; adds latency on small areas (< 20 mm). DistanceThreshold = 0 divides by zero (no guard), never write 0.

Source-verified (tag 0.4.1, plugin manager build for OTD 0.6.1.0-0.6.8.1): IPositionedPipelineElement, PreTransform, one property EMAWeight (UI 'EMA Weight') default 0.5, setter clamps 0..1; 1 = no effect, lower = removes more hardware smoothing. Reverse EMA: out = (current - last) / w + last. w = 0 divides by zero: never write 0. Wiki tuning: start at 0.5, ram the pen into a fixed edge; overshoot -> raise, residual smoothing -> lower; use the minimal value that does not overshoot. Only for tablets with hardware (firmware) smoothing; amplifies noise otherwise. Same math as Temporal Resampler / Saturn 'Reverse EMA' (reverseSmoothing): do not stack them (inference). Adds no latency (it removes it). Not in the plugin manager's per-tablet recommendations; no per-tablet values are published by the author.

Source-verified on main (assumed == v1.1.5, 2026-09-24; plugin manager 1.1.5.0, OTD >= 0.6.7.0; license SUL-1.0, not OSI). PluginName 'A Spectral Reconstructor' (the 'A ' prefix is deliberate so it sorts first in the Filters list, per the v1.1.2 notes). AsyncPositionedPipelineElement, PreTransform. Frequency is re-declared with UI label 'Resampling frequency' (default 1000, clamp 1..4000; 125/250/500/1000 use OTD's native timer, others a fallback timer). LatencySamples is in REPORTS, not ms: latency ~= LatencySamples / report rate (4 samples = ~30 ms at 133 rps, ~5.7 ms at 700 rps); 0 = zero-latency mode with ~50% noise rejection (README). WindowMilliseconds effective clamp 10..500; FilterStrength >= 0 (0 = no filtering; README: 1.5 for 133 Hz tablets; defaults tuned for 700 Hz custom Wacom firmware); OutlierThreshold >= 0.5; StalenessTimeoutMs 1..1000. Very new (first release 2026-09-19) and few community reports: keep advanced.

Exponential smoothing: weight = 1 - 0.37^(1/(Latency/(1000/Frequency))), so the output covers 63% of a step after Latency ms (time constant = Latency). Plugin slider is 0..1000 ms, default 2; its tooltip says below 4 ms you should rather disable it and that ~50 ms is the max for osu!. Frequency (default 1000 Hz) is the filter's own async timer rate inherited from AsyncPositionedPipelineElement, NOT the tablet report rate: this project leaves it at the default.

Base weight reaches 90% of a step within Latency ms (time constant ~ Latency/ln 10). Antichatter divides the weight by y(x) = (x + OffsetX)^(-Strength) * Multiplier + OffsetY where x is distance to the target in mm: slow/small moves get much more smoothing, fast moves fall back to the base weight. Tooltip ranges: Strength 1..10, Multiplier 1..1000, OffsetX -1..2, OffsetY -1..10; presets 'Simple' 5-50 ms / Strength 2-3, 'Smooth' ~10 ms / Strength 3 / Multiplier 100. Prediction (cosh curve) wants >= 10-15 ms of latency. Helps tablets without hardware smoothing. Frequency (default 1000 Hz) is the filter's own async timer rate (AsyncPositionedPipelineElement), NOT the tablet report rate; the tooltip says not to change it, so this project leaves it at the default. source-verified that the base EMA weight (1 - 0.1^(1/steps)) is only computed on the first Filter call, so a Latency change needs the filter to be re-created (Apply/Save) to take effect. Prediction tooltip asks for 10-40 ms of latency and warns it can overshoot. PredictionEnabled has no DefaultPropertyValue attribute (C# default false). If m + OffsetY < 0 the gain becomes 1 (raw passthrough).

Runs at PipelinePosition.Raw. Interpolates between reports (Kalman) so a low-rate tablet (e.g. 133 rps) looks fluid on a high-refresh monitor (README example: 240 Hz). frameShift ('Prediction Ratio') 0 = one report interval of latency, 0.5 = half, 1 = none (works best with some smoothing). latency = Hawku-like EMA in ms. followRadius in mm. reverseSmoothing < 1 undoes hardware smoothing and must be tuned per tablet (Reconstructor guide), so it is left at 1. extraFrames ('Maximize Frequency') default true. The report interval is measured from real report timestamps; Frequency is only used in the stats logger, so this project leaves it at the default. in OTD 0.6.x PipelinePosition.Raw is an alias of PreTransform (same enum value), so TemporalResampler does NOT run before other pre-transform filters; it runs at its position in the settings.json Filters list. Version trap: the plugin manager still lists TemporalResampler 1.0.1 for OTD 0.6.3.0, whose properties were frameShift ('Frame Time Shift'), weight ('EMA Weight', float) and reverseSmoothing as a BOOL; followRadius/latency/extraFrames/loggingEnabled only exist in 1.2.x+. 1.5.1 (listed for OTD >= 0.6.4.0) property names match this catalog exactly (source-verified at tag v1.5.1). latency setter is Math.Max(v,0) (no max); followRadius has no clamp.

Source-verified at tag v0.3.1 (plugin manager 0.3.1.0, OTD 0.6.0.0-0.6.8.1) and unchanged on master. AsyncPositionedPipelineElement, PostTransform (screen pixels). SmoothingFactor (UI 'Pre-interpolation smoothing factor') and TiltSmoothingFactor are EMA weights, default 1 (= no smoothing), setter clamps 0..1 (tooltip says 0.01..1). Draws a quadratic Bezier between midpoints of recent control points, so output trails the newest report by about one report interval plus EMA lag (estimate from code, not measured). Frequency = async output rate, leave at default. It is a resampler: do not stack with Temporal Resampler / Saturn interp / Spectral async (inference).

Source-verified on the default branch (plugin manager 1.1.1, OTD >= 0.6.3.0). WARNING: the settings.json property names are the odd C# names (_getSetScuffedInterpAmount etc.), not the UI labels. AsyncPositionedPipelineElement, PreTransform. Interpolation amount (default 0.5): < 0 forces prediction, 0..1 interpolates/extrapolates, >= 1 smooths. _getScuffedTabletHz is clamped 133..266 and must match the tablet (wrong value 'can break behavior'), so the plugin is only meant for 133-266 rps tablets. _getScuffedLiftResetDelay is in missed reports, min 2. Latency up to ~one report interval scaled by the amount (estimate). Another resampler: do not stack with other async interpolators (inference).

Source-verified on HEAD (plugin manager 1.1.0, OTD >= 0.6.7.0, MIT). AsyncPositionedPipelineElement, PostTransform. All properties are SliderProperty with NO setter clamps. Predicts LookAheadMs + time-since-last-report ahead along a B-spline fit of the last CaptureWindowMs; README admits added jitter. Attribute inconsistencies: D3Strength slider default 0 but DefaultPropertyValue 1 (OTD uses DefaultPropertyValue => 1); IntegrationSteps DefaultPropertyValue 10 but field initializer 30. TabFreq must be the tablet report rate. POLICY: osu! (peppy, 2026-10-14) allows smoothing/anti-jitter plugins but will act on input-assisting plugins; prediction past the pen is not named either way. Never recommend automatically (open question).

Cursor may lag behind the pen by at most OuterRadius (mm here); InnerRadius is a deadzone; SmoothingCoefficient 0.0001..1 (higher = slower descent = more smoothing), default 0.95; SoftKneeScale 0..100 default 1 (roughly logarithmic); SmoothingLeakCoefficient 0..1 default 0. Defaults: OuterRadius 1.0 mm, InnerRadius 0. Fast jumps are not delayed beyond the outer radius, which is why it is popular for osu!. InnerRadius must not exceed OuterRadius. source-verified at tag 0.3.0 (the only build the plugin manager offers for OTD 0.6.0.0-0.6.8.1) and unchanged on master (the 2026-09-09 commit 5fc4af9 only changes the build target framework). settings.json property names are the C# names OuterRadius, InnerRadius, SmoothingCoefficient, SoftKneeScale, SmoothingLeakCoefficient; the UI labels ('Outer Radius', 'Inner Radius', 'Initial Smoothing Coefficient', 'Soft Knee Scale', 'Smoothing Leak Coefficient') are NOT what OTD matches (PluginSettingStore.ApplySettings matches PropertyInfo.Name and silently skips unknown names). PluginName 'AbstractQbit's Radial Follow Smoothing (Tablet coordinates)', PipelinePosition.PreTransform, radii in mm (converted with digitizer Width/MaxX). Core clamps: radii 0..1e6, SmoothingCoefficient 0.0001..1, SoftKneeScale 0..100, SmoothingLeakCoefficient 0..1; effective outer radius = max(Outer, Inner + 0.0001); cursor snaps to the pen after a >= 50 ms report gap or NaN. The 0.1.x line (OTD 0.5 only) had different defaults (Inner 0.05 mm, coefficient 0.92, knee 3).

Same algorithm and the same five C# property names as the tablet-space variant (source-verified at tag 0.3.0). PluginName 'AbstractQbit's Radial Follow Smoothing (Screen coordinates)'; PipelinePosition.Pixels, which is an alias of PostTransform in OTD 0.6.x, so 'post' is correct. Radii in screen pixels: OuterRadius 5.0 px, InnerRadius 0.0 px; coefficient 0.95, knee 1.0, leak 0.0. Pixel radii scale with display/area ratio, so the same px value is a different physical distance for different area sizes.

Plugin manager ships 1.1.0.2 (tag 2026-10-17, OTD >= 0.6.6.2); GitHub latest is 1.1.1.0 (2026-10-23); both have the same 12 properties: reverseSmoothing, stockWeight, rInner, smoothDist (UI 'Distance Smoothing'), sepMult, aResponse, areaScale, xMod, ExGate (UI 'Read Config File': reads SaturnConfig/<Tablet Name>.json in the OTD app folder), interp (default false; it was true in 1.0.0), wireMode, frameShift. dacOuter and msOverride were removed after 1.0.0 (OTD silently ignores them). Frequency is the inherited AsyncPositionedPipelineElement timer rate (default 1000 Hz); MultifilterCore derives expect = 1000/Frequency and compares it with the measured UPDATE interval, i.e. it is the expected update period, not obviously the tablet report period. No Saturn doc says to set Frequency to the report rate, and OTD warns below 101 Hz. Recommendation: leave Frequency at 1000 unless the author confirms otherwise (open question). Tablet-specific tweaks are auto-applied by tablet name (Wacom PTK-x70, PTH-x60, CTL/CTH-x80/x72/x71/x70/x60, PTH-x51/PTK-x40/PTZ, CTL-4100/6100/x90, Gaomon S620).

filters.display_name: Saturn High Report Rate Noise Compensation
filters.notes: Source-verified on main (1.1.1.0, 2026-10-23); the plugin manager ships 1.1.0.2 and the 1.1.1.0 notes say hover-confidence and smoothness/accuracy options were added, so dragDist/maxDist/maxHMult/dragConf may be missing in 1.1.0.2 (unverified). PluginName 'Saturn - High Report Rate Noise Compensation', IPositionedPipelineElement, PreTransform. For very high report rate (modded firmware) tablets; resets history on > 25 ms report gaps, jerk tracker assumes 1000 Hz. Tooltip: it should probably be FIRST in the filter chain. noiseAmount unit not stated (raw tablet units inferred); hover distances are raw HoverDistance values from the Tablet Debugger. Setter minimums: noiseAmount >= 0, posSlack >= 1, cStrength 0..1, TimingSeverity >= 0 (tooltip: leave 0, else 1-3), crossSeverity >= 0, vMult 0..1, timeScale >= 0, maxHMult >= 1, dragConf >= 1. Max values here are project tuning bounds, not plugin limits. Not useful on 133-266 rps tablets.

Post-transform reshaping by distance from the display center (not a smoothing filter, adds no latency). threshold = radius where output equals input (screen px); dPower > 1 expands, < 1 shrinks; useful range ~0.5..2. Never recommended automatically; listed so existing profiles can be understood.

Source-verified: PostTransform (screen pixels), DefaultPropertyValue 2. Per report: d = |input - last|, m = max(((-d + (S - 1.7)) / 1.96)^19 + 30, 0), gain = clamp(0.9 / m, 0, 1), last += delta * gain. Below ~S + 0.6 px the gain is ~0.03 per report (heavy smoothing, lag grows at low report rates); above it the gain jumps to 1 (raw). No buffering, no async timer. Tooltip: 2-3 dragging, 5-6 hovering, any value > 0.

Source-verified: PreTransform, DefaultPropertyValue 6, same formula as RAW. No millimetre conversion is visible in the source, so distances are raw tablet units (inferred: the strength therefore means a different physical distance on tablets with different LPI). Tooltip: 6-7 dragging, 15-16 hovering. Community osu! preset for CTL-472 (hover play) uses 15.

Source-verified on main (0.1.4.0, OTD >= 0.6.8.0; 0.1.3.0 for 0.6.4-0.6.7). Not a smoothing filter: it DROPS reports outside a HoverDistance / pressure window (adds no latency). Uses the new PipelinePosition.Internal (OTD 0.6.8+), which runs before ALL PreTransform filters; this catalog has no 'internal' stage, so 'raw' is used as the closest (engine should map it to 'run first'). Hover_min/Hover_max/Pressure_min/Pressure_max are ints in the tablet's raw HoverDistance / pressure units (read them in Tablets > Tablet debugger; HoverDistance is not reported by every tablet). Boolean properties have no DefaultPropertyValue (C# false). Typical osu! use (prose, unverified): cut the noisy far-hover range. Never recommend automatically.
